text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000129 bills 99215 far above expectation in every complexity tier, but the few returned charts support the billed levels, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 rate is not explained by a sicker panel: it appears in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215 visits for simple problems such as follow-up (Z09: C0057524, C0057567, C0057790), URI (C0057778) and UTI (C0057378, C0057647). Against that, none of the 13 documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, and notes like C0057320 and C0057758 record high MDM with substantial time, which points toward legitimate complexity. That documentation is thin, though, covering about 5% of claims, and some note-signal flags (problem-list and data flags, and the 5 moderate-plus data notes with no lab or test line on the claim) are weak signs that notes could be templated or inflated to match the billed code; C0057675 is supported at high MDM with no time recorded and carries a data flag. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above, along with the EHR audit trail that was not received, to see whether the high-MDM documentation reflects work actually performed or cloned content."}
